$comment: Rule catalog — open problems and the research lifecycle. Standards 17, 18. Two categories share this file: problems and lifecycle.

rules.title: Each open problem has a tracking file
rules.description: When the policy declares openProblemMode, at least one artifacts/open-problems/<slug>/problem.md exists and carries all nine required sections of Standard 17 R1.
rules.rationale: On a famous problem the incentive to read partial progress generously is at its maximum, and the sections are the questions that resist that reading.
rules.remediation: Create the file from templates/open-problem.md and answer every section. An empty section is a finding; `none` written deliberately is an answer.
rules.$assuranceNote: Exact about the file and its headings. Headings existing is not the analysis being honest.

rules.title: What is proved is stated separately from what is conjectural
rules.description: The What Is Proved and What Remains Conjectural sections are both present and non-empty.
rules.rationale: A project that cannot state in one sentence what it has actually proved about the target has learned something important about its own position. Frequently the honest content of the first section is 'nothing about the target itself', and writing that is the most valuable line in the document.
rules.remediation: List the claims at proved rank with their identifiers, with conditional results carrying their conditions. State plainly where the target is untouched.
rules.$assuranceNote: Establishes that both sections say something. It does not cross-check them against the ledger's statuses, and it cannot tell an honest summary from an optimistic one.

rules.title: The problem file records what is already known
rules.description: The Known Results section records the literature comparison, including prior attempts on this approach and why they stopped.
rules.rationale: For a major problem, an approach that appears new to the project has usually been tried, and the reasons it stopped are the most useful information available.
rules.remediation: Search specifically for prior attempts, not only for the result, and record what was found.
rules.$assuranceNote: Establishes that the section is populated. The competence of the search is review.

rules.title: Equivalence to the target is recorded with direction
rules.description: The Equivalences section records each relationship to the target with its direction — implies, implied-by, or iff — and the proof status of the relationship itself.
rules.rationale: A statement equivalent to the target is exactly as unproved as the target, whatever it looks like, and asserting iff where one direction is proved is a silent strengthening.
rules.remediation: Record each relationship with its direction and the claim that proves it.
rules.$assuranceNote: Establishes that the section is populated. Whether an asserted equivalence holds is mathematics.

rules.title: The location of the central difficulty is stated
rules.description: The Where the Difficulty Lives section names, in plain language, what the hard part currently is, and what moved it when it has changed.
rules.rationale: Requiring the sentence to be written is most of the value. A project that cannot say where the difficulty is has usually not moved it.
rules.remediation: Write the sentence. Where the difficulty has moved, say what moved it and why that is a reduction rather than a relabelling.
rules.$assuranceNote: Establishes that the section is non-empty. Whether the answer is honest is proof.difficulty-displacement, which has no detector.

rules.title: Known barriers are recorded
rules.description: The Known Barriers section records each barrier encountered, its citation, and which approaches it rules out.
rules.rationale: Barriers are results about which approaches cannot work. Pursuing an approach after its barrier is documented is the clearest available signal that the record is not being read.
rules.remediation: Record the barrier with its citation and the approaches it excludes.
rules.$assuranceNote: Establishes that the section exists and says something. It cannot know which barriers apply to this problem.

rules.title: A restatement of the conjecture is never a solution
rules.description: A restatement of the central conjecture is described as solving it.
rules.rationale: This is the maximum-strength form of presenting a reformulation as progress, and the failure an agent asked to make progress on a famous problem is most likely to produce, because producing something that looks like progress is a far easier target than progress.
rules.remediation: Record the restatement as an EQUIVALENT_REFORMULATION with its direction, leave the target's status where it was, and say what the restatement makes newly available.
rules.$assuranceNote: No detector. The structural signal — the target's status stays capped by its dependency closure — is caught by claims.status-exceeds-support, but the claim of having solved the problem lives in prose and its assessment is mathematical.

rules.title: Failed research routes are preserved
rules.description: The project retains a location recording routes that were tried and abandoned, with what was tried and what happened.
rules.rationale: Deleting a failed route destroys the reason not to repeat it, the negative evidence it produced, and the ability of anyone to see the shape of the search — which is what makes selective reporting visible at all.
rules.remediation: Keep abandoned work in research/abandoned/ or in dated notes. Preserved does not mean prominent; removal is what is prohibited.
rules.$assuranceNote: Looks for a preserved-failure location. It cannot detect a deletion — nothing in a repository's current state reveals what was removed, and a check claiming otherwise would be inventing a capability.

rules.title: Terminated approaches record why they stopped
rules.description: Each terminated approach carries a Status line with its date and the reason it stopped.
rules.rationale: Termination is a decision, and a decision with no record is indistinguishable from having drifted away from the work.
rules.remediation: Add the Status line with the date and the reason, referencing the claims or notes that establish it.
rules.$assuranceNote: Establishes that the line is present. The truthfulness of the reason is review.

rules.title: Terminated approaches state what would reopen them
rules.description: Each terminated approach carries an 'Evidence required to reopen' line naming a specific, checkable condition.
rules.rationale: It turns 'we gave up on this' into a falsifiable condition, and it is the difference between a closed direction and one that reopens whenever morale improves — a loop an untiring agent is far more prone to than a person.
rules.remediation: Name the specific result, bound, or technique whose appearance would justify revisiting the approach.
rules.$assuranceNote: Establishes that the line is present and non-empty. Whether the condition is specific enough to be checkable is review.

rules.title: Stopping criteria are stated in advance
rules.description: The research effort records what would make it stop: a barrier, a resource bound, a date, or a literature result that would settle the question.
rules.rationale: Criteria written at the start are a research plan; criteria written at the end are a description of what happened. An effort that cannot say what would make it stop has no way to distinguish persistence from sunk cost.
rules.remediation: Write the Stopping Criteria section before the work begins, with specific and checkable conditions.
rules.$assuranceNote: Establishes that the section is non-empty. It cannot establish that the criteria were written in advance rather than reconstructed, which only the commit history shows.
